detail: Go to business.facebook.com and create a Business Manager account if you don't already have one (use Klaargesukkel's business details, not personal).

In Business Settings, go to Business Info and start Business Verification — you'll need a business document (CIPC registration, or similar SA business proof) and it can take several days to process, so start this first.
Once verified, go to developers.facebook.com, create a new App, add the 'WhatsApp' product to it.
In the app's WhatsApp > API Setup page, note the temporary access token, the phone number ID, and the WhatsApp Business Account ID — these get handed to Claude Code when the new repo/session starts.
For a permanent (non-expiring) token, generate a System User token in Business Settings > System Users instead of using the temporary one.

name: EyeSpy
description: Demand-signal research tool — reads compliant sources (Reddit API, search API, Google Places reviews, RSS, open data, podcast) plus weekly manual Facebook Group screenshot capture for a region, tracks recurring themes over time, surfaces trends to feed product ideation.
location: apps/ops (/eyespy, /eyespy/[themeId], /eyespy/capture, /eyespy/sources), this repo — live and pulling real signals from 10 sources: IOL RSS, GroundUp Q&A RSS, GroundUp News RSS, Daily Maverick RSS, CapeTalk consumer podcast, Cape Town Service Requests (ArcGIS), Google Search, Brave Search, Google Places (business reviews), plus manual Facebook Group capture. Every signal is classified demand/supply/unclear, with trend/volume counting demand only. Reddit built but blocked on an account hold (see next steps). Google Trends alpha still open (low priority).

nextSteps.step: Run the cron a handful more times (Vercel → Cron Jobs → Run) to finish backfilling signal_type on existing signals — built 2026-08-02: a demand/supply/unclear field is now classified in the same Claude pass, trend/volume math only counts demand, and the theme detail page has a signal-type filter (defaults to demand, supply/unclear/all still viewable as context). The bad Brave-ad batch was already deleted by hand. Capped at 40 classifications per run to avoid the earlier timeout, so ~13-14 runs are needed to fully backfill all existing signals — themes will show low/zero counts until then, that's expected, not a bug
detail: Migration apps/ops/prisma/migrations/20260802140000_add_signal_type/migration.sql needs hand-applying via the Query tool first if not already done.
Full spec in EYESPY.md's Data sources (search-API caveat), Processing (step 3b/4), and Output (signal_type filter + backfill note) sections.

nextSteps.step: Blocked 2026-08-02: Reddit is showing Albert's account "blocked by network security" on reddit.com/prefs/apps — reproduced across a different browser (Edge) and a different network (phone on mobile data), so it looks like an account-level hold rather than anything fixable on our end. Ticket filed with Reddit. Parked, not urgent — everything else (RSS, ArcGIS, Google, Brave, manual capture) is live without it. lib/ingest/reddit.ts is already built and wired in (client_credentials OAuth, r/CapeTown + r/southafrica search for "Durbanville"), just needs REDDIT_CLIENT_ID/REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET once the account is unblocked
nextSteps.waitingOn: Reddit's account hold clearing (could be hours to a couple days) — no need to keep retrying, it won't speed it up

nextSteps.step: Parked 2026-08-02: Google Search (geo+intent) is active but returning zero signals — its Programmable Search Engine is still restricted to 4 specific sites (facebook.com, gumtree.co.za, hellopeter.com, reddit.com) since the "search the entire web" toggle never worked in Google's UI (see earlier troubleshooting). Brave Search is doing the equivalent job without that restriction (99 signals, working fine), so Albert decided not to keep chasing Google's config — left active as-is, not a bug to fix, just redundant. Revisit only if Brave ever gets throttled/removed
Provide Google Places API key
detail: Go to console.cloud.google.com, select the same project used for Search (or create one).
Go to APIs & Services > Library, search for 'Places API', click Enable.
Go to APIs & Services > Credentials, click Create Credentials > API Key, copy it.
Consider restricting the key to the Places API only under the key's settings, for safety.

nextSteps.step: Apply for Google Trends API (alpha) access — new official API (launched July 2025), free for approved testers, gives quantified search-intent data to cross-check qualitative sources. Not urgent, approval timeline unknown
